734707549f64c4a6624a.text: As the Oxford Languages dictionary defines it, a Parable is a simple story used

9a78c88e74492de35cc6.text: to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson, as told by Jesus in the Gospels. It is a type of metaphorical analogy that involves figures of speech specifically symbolism – metaphors and simile – all to explain a separate meaning from its literal definition to make the comparison clearer and to give stronger impact to the reader.

3d06660cda9bf261d3c7.text: 1. Metaphor - A metaphor is an implicit comparison of one thing to another without the use of a commonly known sign or equation. A subcategory of metaphors is "personification," attributing a human characteristic—or emotion— to an animal, object, or concept. Example: The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.

5d8b064b6dcd72eb1b3a.text: Simile - it explicitly denotes a comparison. A simile very often uses either the word like or as. Example: “The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field.”

5f65520e7e032c9283e9.text: 3. Allegory - An allegory is very similar to a metaphor in the sense that something—usually something abstract or religious—is implicitly articulated in terms of something else that is concrete. The difference between an allegory and a metaphor is that when an allegory is employed, the comparison reflects the entire work—or a large part of the work. Example: The seed mentioned in the parable is interpreted as the Word of God.

fca0eff1fe522ce3ad64.text: Archetype – a collectively inherited unconscious idea, pattern of thought, image, etc., a model or first form. Example: Melchizidek, king of Salem meaning peace, is an archetype of Christ Myth – a traditional or legendary story usually concerning some being or hero or event with or without determinable basis of fact or a natural explanation.

151ff194bdac1c69f200.text: Example: The Moon Goddess; Pandora’s Box; Si Malakas at si Maganda

8e7580705ea6c7dec9bb.text: Is the Parable of the Sower a Myth? What makes you say it’s an Allegory? Can you quote an example of metaphors? How about simile?

ab9e9f81a29661fd206a.text: An example of Archetype is our picture that comes to mind when we think of

cd7c43e4bcbf47b2f198.text: the devil – a monstrous, frightening humanoid with two big horns on the head. Contrarily, the Bible described the devil in Genesis as taking the form of a snake, telling lies to Adam & Eve. It actually does not explain how it looked like, but rather, what he does – a liar.

4a3ca996cd10effe9f19.text: Jesus told these stories with heavenly meanings (Parables) because He knew

e0574f0286e177d67797.text: that people actually do not listen to direct instructions because by nature we are bad and will only react more from stories that are baseless rumors.

9cc344645196fb0a59f2.text: In this trying time, we need to focus more on the lesson more important than

882443a4b61ff59108aa.text: what meets the eye. Faith, therefore, is not something we do to have it in the first place. It is a gift from God. This Symbolism will assist us in unlocking the true meaning of the Parables. Let’s learn more on the next page.
